URL: https://edition.cnn.com/2026/11/17/europe/ukraine-russia-kerch-bridge-intl-hnk
CNN, 17 Nov 2026

The Crimean Bridge, also known as the Kerch Bridge, is a vital supply line for Moscow’s troops and has huge symbolic value for Russian President Vladimir Putin, who made its construction a key priority after Russia’s illegal annexation of the Ukrainian peninsula in 2014.

Ukraine has stepped up its attacks against Crimea in the past six months, forcing the Russian-installed authorities to impose a state of emergency over the summer because of widespread power outages and fuel shortages on the heavily militarized peninsula.

The timing of the latest attack, on the eve of Putin’s meeting with US President Donald Trump and Chinese leader Xi Jinping in Asia, makes it even more symbolic.

The Kremlin has sought to frame the gathering as a “New Yalta” in a nod to the 1945 conference at which Soviet leader Joseph Stalin effectively redrew the global map of spheres of influence with the Allied powers. The attack on the bridge makes Yalta, a city in annexed Crimea, effectively inaccessible from mainland Russia, at least until it is repaired.

An image shared on social media and verified by CNN shows a section of the Kerch bridge collapsed in the water.
    
  
          pravdaGerashchenko_en/Telegram
        
      
    
    



      
    
       
    
    
    
    
      
        
          
          
    
    The bridge pictured in its complete state before the attacks, on July 17, 2023.
    
  
          Alexey Pavlishak/Reuters
        
      
    
    


    
            “It is of fundamental importance: The strike was carried out exclusively with Ukrainian weapons – using our technologies and our solutions,” Ukrainian Defense Minister Yevhenii Khmara said.

Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky also confirmed Tuesday that domestically manufactured missiles and drones were used in the attack, including Neptune missiles that he said struck the railway section of the bridge and Palianytsia drones that targeted the road section.

“Today, at the key stage, the ‘Palianytsia’ drones performed exceptionally well, striking the road section of the bridge, while ‘Neptune’ missiles, ‘Ruta’ drones, and FP-5 drones struck the railway section,” Zelensky said in a statement posted on X.

Zelensky said the strike was the seventh stage of what he called “an unprecedented operation in response to Russian strikes on our infrastructure.”

“As a result of the strikes, one of the metal arches and the road span beneath it were completely destroyed,” said Ukraine’s Security Service, the SBU, adding that the railway section of the bridge was also “preliminarily damaged.”

Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov sought to play down the impact of the attack, saying the bridge would be rebuilt “even better than before,” according to Russian state news agency TASS, citing the Izvestia newspaper.

The $3.7 billion bridge, which at nearly 12 miles is the longest crossing in Europe, was built to handle 40,000 cars a day and move 14 million passengers and 13 million tons of cargo per year, according to Russian state media.

Videos and images geolocated by CNN appear to show a portion of the road bridge collapsed into the water. The parallel rail bridge appeared still to be standing. In another video geolocated by CNN, a fire can be seen burning on a section of the bridge.

A Ukrainian woman walks down a street, as anti-Drone nets are strung up over main Ukrainian roads and towns in eastern Ukraine and the Donbas region, to protect from Russian FPV (First-Person View) drones that can fly far beyond front-line positions to create a 20-mile-deep kill zone on each side of the front, on July 19, 2026 in Sloviansk, Ukraine. Ubiquitous drone use by both sides, sometime connected by hair-thin fiber optic cables to defeat electronic jamming, have transformed the battlefield since Russia's all-out invasion of Ukraine in 2022.
    
  
          Scott Peterson/Getty Images
        
      
    
    


    
    
      
        US floated idea of Ukraine swapping land for NATO membership, Zelensky says

Traffic has been suspended following the second Ukrainian attack in as many days, Russia’s transport ministry said, adding that the bridge was damaged in a drone attack.

“Experts are assessing the damage,” said the ministry, adding that there were no casualties.

Railway traffic across the bridge has since resumed, according to TASS. Moscow-backed Crimea governor Sergei Aksyonov said passengers without vehicles could also use a ferry crossing.

Russia’s Investigative Committee confirmed the attack on the bridge, calling it a “terrorist act by Ukrainian armed groups.”

Ukraine has repeatedly targeted the Kerch Bridge since Russia’s full-scale invasion began in 2022, but the damage the bridge sustained this week appears to be more significant than in some of the previous attacks.

Russia’s military said its air defenses had shot down 1,441 Ukrainian drones overnight.

A worker looks at the destruction of the Southern Bridge after a Russian strike in Kyiv, Ukraine, on Tuesday.
    
  
          Evgeniy Maloletka/AP
        
      
    
    


    
            The Ukrainian capital Kyiv also came under intense bombardment overnight into Tuesday. Two people were killed and the city’s North and South bridges badly damaged in the assault, officials said.

“Last night, four ballistic missiles struck the Southern Bridge and three struck the Northern Bridge,” Zelensky said in a separate statement on X.

Kyiv is split in half by the Dnipro River. The right bank is home to the majority of the city’s business centers, offices and government institutions, while the left bank is mostly residential.

The bridges connecting the two sides are crucial – some 600,000 vehicles as well as trains and Kyiv’s metro cross them every day.

“Critical infrastructure systems have been damaged, causing disruptions to water and heat supply in some districts,” the city office said.

Russia's President Vladimir Putin, accompanied by Kremlin foreign policy adviser Yuri Ushakov, meets with US envoys at the Kremlin in Moscow on November 12, 2026.
    
  
          Vyacheslav Prokofyev/Pool/AFP/Getty Images
        
      
    
    


    
    
      
        Europe and Ukraine get a boost in peace talks, but Putin is playing for time

Zelensky also confirmed “significant” power outages in the Dnipro, Kharkiv and Zaporizhzhia regions, saying emergency and repair crews were working to deal with the consequences of the Russian strike on the power grid.

The attacks on the bridges have led to major traffic jams on both the left and right banks, although the scale of damage was still being clarified, officials said.

Russia’s military said it had targeted Ukrainian military, transportation, energy and port infrastructure, using drones and ground- and air-based precision-guided weapons.

The exchange of attacks on critical infrastructure come two days before the planned trilateral talks between Trump, Xi and Putin in Shenzhen, China on the sidelines of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) leaders’ summit.

Trump said Monday he expects to discuss the war in Ukraine with his Russian and Chinese counterparts, despite US officials suggesting last week the topic wouldn’t be on the table.

US President Donald Trump salutes during a ceremony in honor of Veterans Day at Arlington National Cemetery in Virginia, on November 11.
    
  
          Kevin Dietsch/Getty Images
        
      
    
    


    
    
      
        How Trump is hoping to use an Asia trip to reassert his authority

“We’ll talk about my favorite subject, Ukraine,” Trump told reporters as he departed the White House.

“Ukraine’s losing – Ukraine-Russia is losing 25,000 soldiers a month, so we’ll be talking about that,” he said, without giving any source for that claim. NATO Secretary General Mark Rutte said last week that Russia was losing “more than 40,000 troops – killed or seriously wounded – every month.”

Peskov said the recent attacks by Kyiv could be linked to the upcoming trilateral meeting, according to Russian state media outlet Vesti, but provided no evidence to support the claim.

In October, Zelensky voiced concern that a trilateral meeting between Trump, Xi and Putin might lead to dealmaking about the future of Ukraine without Kyiv being consulted.

CNN’s Kevin Liptak and Daria Tarasova-Markina contributed reporting.
